c.tagline: A sprawling Red Sea resort city with reef-fringed islands, diving, and Egypt's largest aquarium
langs: German and Russian (common due to tourism)

card: Widely accepted at hotels and larger restaurants; cash useful for El Dahar market and taxis

taxi.fare: Negotiated flat rate, as meters are uncommon
taxi.fareNote: Agree the fare before departure; hotel-arranged transfers are common

emergency.note: Tourist police (180) can assist with English-language support

english.label: Easy to get by in English

walk: Sekalla and El Mamsha waterfront strips are walkable; El Dahar and other districts require a taxi given the city's sprawl

safety.safety: Generally safe in the resort and tourist zones, with a visible tourist police presence
safety.crime: Petty theft and persistent vendors/touts in markets are the main practical concerns

hood_landmark.El Dahar: El Dahar's traditional souks and Al Mina Mosque
hood_landmark.Sekalla (El Saqqala): Sekalla's busy Sheraton Road hotel and shopping strip
hood_landmark.El Ahyaa: El Ahyaa's residential and mid-range resort area
hood_landmark.Giftun Islands (day-trip): The protected Giftun Islands snorkeling reefs

avoid.reason: Expect aggressive touts, taxi overcharging, and dive/excursion booking scams in Sheraton Road and El Dahar bazaar areas — agree prices in advance.

hood_desc: The oldest part of Hurghada, with traditional bazaars, cheaper eats, and the long-distance bus station.
The historic tourist core along Sheraton Road, packed with hotels, shops, and restaurants.
A newer waterfront strip north of Sekalla with more contemporary hotels, restaurants, and shops.
A quieter, more residential district with mid-range and budget resorts, less central than Sekalla.
A cluster of protected coral islands a short boat ride offshore, essential for snorkeling and diving day trips.

water.note: Drink bottled water only; avoid ice of unknown origin outside resorts.

transit.sys: Local minibuses along the main coastal road; hotel shuttles common
transit.hours: Minibuses run roughly daylight to evening hours
transit.map: Not centrally published; ask locally for minibus routes
transit.note: Most visitors rely on taxis or hotel-arranged transport given the city's spread-out layout

transport.air: Hurghada International Airport (HRG), about 15-20 min from Sekalla
transport.train: No passenger rail service to Hurghada
transport.bus: Long-distance buses connect to Cairo, Luxor, and other Egyptian cities
transport.ferry: Seasonal boats connect to Sharm El Sheikh across the Red Sea
transport.car: Rental cars available; most visitors use taxis and hotel transfers

net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ops: Vodafone Egypt, Orange Egypt, Etisalat Misr
net.fwn: Free wifi widely available in hotels
net.ap: A Vodafone or Orange Egypt tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: 10-15% is customary for dive guides and tour operators
tip.r: 10% is standard, though often added automatically at resort restaurants
